GTAVOnline.Description: Grand Theft Auto V Enhanced / GTA Online on Nobara via Steam + Proton — Steam AppID 3240220 (the old 'GTA V Legacy' is 271590; set "appid" to that if you run the legacy copy). GTA Online is driven by BattlEye anti-cheat, so the prefix has to carry the Proton BattlEye Runtime and a recent GE-Proton, and BattlEye's servers have to be blocked in /etc/hosts (step 6b). That gets GTA Online into closed crew / closed friend / invite-only sessions; public sessions still kick you. Work through the steps top to bottom: the ones with a Run button do the work for you; the manual ones are quick clicks inside Steam that can't be scripted. This mirrors README “GTA V Online → Route A”.

steps.title: 1 · Install Steam (native)
steps.desc: Native RPM Steam (RPM Fusion) — the SteamOS-style setup where Steam manages Proton and the Linux Runtime containers itself. A Flatpak Steam is deliberately not used here (its sandbox complicates controller access, game drives and the MangoHud / gamescope / vkBasalt layers).

steps.title: 2 · Install GameMode, MangoHud, vkBasalt, gamescope
steps.desc: Per-game performance profile (GameMode), the FPS/frametime overlay (MangoHud + GOverlay to configure it), post-process layer (vkBasalt) and the gamescope micro-compositor. Also adds you to the gamemode group.
steps.check: rpm -q gamemode mangohud vkBasalt gamescope goverlay >/dev/null 2>&1
steps.run: dnf install -y gamemode mangohud vkBasalt gamescope goverlay && usermod -aG gamemode {USER}

steps.title: 3 · Install Protontricks
steps.desc: winetricks for Steam/Proton prefixes — used later to drop vcrun2019 / d3dcompiler_47 / corefonts into GTA V's prefix and to flip the prefix to Windows 10 if the Rockstar / Social Club sign-in loops.
steps.check: rpm -q protontricks >/dev/null 2>&1 || sudo -u {USER} flatpak info com.github.Matoking.protontricks >/dev/null 2>&1

steps.title: 4 · Install ProtonUp-Qt
steps.desc: GUI to manage GE-Proton / wine-GE versions per launcher. Installed as a Flatpak for {USER}. You can use it instead of step 5 if you prefer clicking.
steps.check: flatpak info net.davidotek.pupgui2 >/dev/null 2>&1 || sudo -u {USER} flatpak info net.davidotek.pupgui2 >/dev/null 2>&1
steps.run: dnf install -y flatpak && flatpak remote-add --if-not-exists flathub https://flathub.org/repo/flathub.flatpakrepo && sudo -u {USER} flatpak install -y --noninteractive flathub net.davidotek.pupgui2

steps.title: 5 · Install the latest GE-Proton
steps.desc: Downloads the newest GloriousEggroll GE-Proton release straight from GitHub and unpacks it into Steam's compatibilitytools.d for {USER}. Restart Steam afterwards so it shows up under Compatibility.
steps.run: su - {USER} -c 'set -e; d="$HOME/.local/share/Steam/compatibilitytools.d"; [ -d "$HOME/.steam/root" ] && d="$HOME/.steam/root/compatibilitytools.d"; mkdir -p "$d"; url=$(curl -fsSL https://api.github.com/repos/GloriousEggroll/proton-ge-custom/releases/latest | grep -oP "https://[^\x22]+GE-Proton[^\x22]+tar[.]gz" | head -1); test -n "$url"; echo "Downloading $url"; curl -fL "$url" -o /tmp/geproton.tar.gz; tar -xzf /tmp/geproton.tar.gz -C "$d"; rm -f /tmp/geproton.tar.gz; echo "compatibilitytools.d now holds:"; ls -1 "$d"'

steps.title: 5b · Keep the Proton prefix off NTFS / exFAT
steps.desc: If GTA V lives on an NTFS or exFAT drive (common for a shared Windows game library), Proton can't build its prefix there — creating the drive-letter links dies with 'OSError: [Errno 22] … dosdevices/s:' because those filesystems reject ':' in a filename (ntfs3 'windows_names'), so the game never starts. Run step keeps the game where it is but moves just AppID {APPID}'s prefix onto your Linux drive and symlinks it back. Close Steam / the game first, then re-launch to rebuild the prefix cleanly. No-op if the game is already on a Linux filesystem.

steps.title: 6 · Install the Proton BattlEye Runtime
steps.desc: GTA Online's BattlEye only loads if this Steam tool (app 1161040) is present. This triggers the install; Steam will open. If it doesn't take, install “Proton BattlEye Runtime” from your Steam Library → Tools list by hand.

steps.title: 6b · Block BattlEye's servers in /etc/hosts
steps.desc: Without this, GTA Online connects and BattlEye kicks you shortly after joining. Pointing paradiseenhanced-s1, paradise-s1 (GTA V Legacy) and test-s1 .battleye.com at 0.0.0.0 lets GTA Online load into closed crew / closed friend / invite-only sessions; PUBLIC sessions still kick you (“kicked by BattlEye”) — that part is server-side and no local fix changes it. Backs /etc/hosts up first. Remove the lines again to undo. Restart Steam (or reboot) afterwards so nothing keeps a cached lookup. Known quirk: opening the Steam overlay in-game can kill all game input until you restart the game — avoid Shift+Tab.
steps.run: cp -a /etc/hosts /etc/hosts.bak-gtav && grep -q '^# GTA V Online on Proton: BattlEye block' /etc/hosts || printf '\n# GTA V Online on Proton: BattlEye block (closed crew/friend/invite-only sessions)\n' >> /etc/hosts; for h in paradiseenhanced-s1 paradise-s1 test-s1; do grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*0\.0\.0\.0[[:space:]]+$h\.battleye\.com([[:space:]]|\$)" /etc/hosts || { c=''; [ $h = paradise-s1 ] && c=' # GTA V Legacy Online'; echo "0.0.0.0 $h.battleye.com$c" >> /etc/hosts; }; done; grep battleye /etc/hosts

steps.title: 7 · Raise vm.max_map_count
steps.desc: Modern Proton titles (and GTA V with mods) can exhaust the default mmap limit and crash on load. Writes a persistent /etc/sysctl.d/80-gtav.conf and applies it now. Nobara often sets this already — the step is a no-op then.

steps.title: 8 · Apply the network-latency tweaks
steps.desc: GTA Online is sensitive to Wi-Fi latency spikes. Applies WifiPowersaveOff (kills the Wi-Fi power-save that causes stutter), NetLatencySysctl (TCP/qdisc tuning) and GamingResourceLimits (higher file-descriptor / RT limits) via apply_tweak.py.
steps.run: for t in WifiPowersaveOff NetLatencySysctl GamingResourceLimits; do echo "### apply_tweak $t"; python3 {TOOLKIT_DIR}/apply_tweak.py "$t" || true; done

steps.title: 9 · Enable Steam Play for all titles  (manual)
steps.desc: In Steam: Settings → Compatibility → turn on “Enable Steam Play for all other titles” and pick the GE-Proton from step 5. Restart Steam when it asks. This can't be scripted safely while Steam is running.

steps.title: 10 · Force GE-Proton on GTA V  (manual)
steps.desc: Steam Library → right-click Grand Theft Auto V → Properties → Compatibility → tick “Force the use of a specific Steam Play compatibility tool” → choose the GE-Proton from step 5. GTA Online needs GE-Proton — Valve's Proton / Proton Experimental don't get past BattlEye.

steps.title: 11 · Set the launch options  (manual)
steps.desc: Properties → General → Launch Options. Paste the string below (Copy button). PROTON_BATTLEYE_RUNTIME points GE-Proton at the BattlEye Runtime from step 6 (absolute path, quoted because of the spaces — a quoted ~ does NOT expand, so don't shorten it to ~/…). It keeps the Vulkan layer stack CLEAN for BattlEye — MANGOHUD=0 + DISABLE_VKBASALT=1 + VK_LOADER_LAYERS_DISABLE=~implicit~ turn off every injected implicit layer (overlay / post-fx), which is what avoids anti-cheat bans and startup crashes; gamemoderun is a plain wrapper (not a layer) so it stays. The three __…OFFLOAD / optimus / GLX vars render on the NVIDIA dGPU — drop them if you've switched to nvidia-only graphics mode (Power & Limits → hybrid graphics). DXVK_ASYNC=1 cuts shader-compile stutter (GE-Proton's DXVK supports it). Want a persistent shader cache too? build the string on the Game Tools tab after setting a cache folder. BattlEye installs itself into the prefix on the first launch — let it finish, then start the game again.
steps.copy: PROTON_BATTLEYE_RUNTIME="/home/{USER}/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/common/Proton BattlEye Runtime" __NV_PRIME_RENDER_OFFLOAD=1 __VK_LAYER_NV_optimus=NVIDIA_only __GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME=nvidia MANGOHUD=0 DISABLE_VKBASALT=1 VK_LOADER_LAYERS_DISABLE=~implicit~ DXVK_ASYNC=1 gamemoderun %command%

steps.title: 12 · Rockstar launcher / Social Club deps  (manual)
steps.desc: Only needed if the Rockstar Games Launcher or Social Club sign-in is black, blank or loops. Launch GTA V once first so Proton creates the prefix, quit, then run the command below (Copy) — it drops vcrun2019, d3dcompiler_47 and corefonts into AppID {APPID}'s prefix non-interactively. Use `protontricks {APPID} --gui` instead if you also need to flip the prefix to Windows 10.

steps.title: 13 · First launch  (manual)
steps.desc: Start GTA V from Steam. First launch pulls in BattlEye and the Rockstar Games Launcher inside the prefix — let it finish, then start the game again. If Social Club still misbehaves, do step 12; if a window stays black, try a different GE-Proton version (step 5 / ProtonUp-Qt).

GTA3DE.Description: Grand Theft Auto III – The Definitive Edition on Nobara via Steam + Proton — Steam AppID 1546970. It boots through the Rockstar Games Launcher (like GTA V Enhanced), so it needs a recent GE-Proton and the Proton prefix kept off NTFS/exFAT (tuxthrottle_prefix_relocate.py); if the launcher / Social Club sign-in loops or renders black, drop vcrun2019 / d3dcompiler_47 / corefonts into the prefix and set it to Windows 10. It is single-player (no BattlEye), so the clean-Vulkan-layer launch string GTA Online needs isn't required — a plain gamemoderun mangohud %command% (+ PRIME offload on the hybrid G15) is enough. steps.title: 10 · First launch  (manual)
steps.desc: Start GTA San Andreas Definitive from Steam. First launch pulls in the Rockstar Games Launcher inside the prefix — let it finish, then start the game again. If Social Club still misbehaves, do step 9; if a window stays black, try a different GE-Proton version (step 5 / ProtonUp-Qt).

SWBF2Classic.Description: Star Wars Battlefront II (2005) — the Classic release on Steam, AppID 6060 — via Proton. It's a 32-bit DirectX 9 title from 2005 with no anti-cheat, so it doesn't need the BattlEye/EAC handling the GTA entries do — a plain gamemoderun mangohud %command% (+ PRIME offload on the hybrid G15) is normally enough. CONFIRMED on the G15 (2026-09-14, Proton Experimental, NVIDIA driver 595.91.07): the loading screen flashes then the game dies with `err:vulkan:vkDestroySwapchainKHR Exception 0xc0000005 in Unix call` inside `libnvidia-glcore.so`, right after DXVK logs `Presenter: Got VK_SUBOPTIMAL_KHR, recreating swapchain` — the game's window grows from its initial 800×600 Vulkan surface to the real desktop size, and NVIDIA's 32-bit proprietary driver segfaults recreating the swapchain for that resize, inside the Steam Linux Runtime container. Step 9 below (gamescope) fixes this by giving the game one fixed-size surface so that resize never happens; step 10 (wined3d) is the fallback if gamescope isn't enough — it bypasses DXVK/Vulkan for this title's D3D9 renderer entirely. Work through the steps top to bottom: the ones with a Run button do the work for you; the manual ones are quick clicks inside Steam that can't be scripted.

steps.title: 1 · Install Steam (native)
steps.desc: Native RPM Steam (RPM Fusion) — the SteamOS-style setup where Steam manages Proton and the Linux Runtime containers itself. A Flatpak Steam is deliberately not used here (its sandbox complicates controller access, game drives and the MangoHud / gamescope / vkBasalt layers).

steps.title: 2 · Install GameMode, MangoHud, vkBasalt, gamescope
steps.desc: Per-game performance profile (GameMode), the FPS/frametime overlay (MangoHud + GOverlay to configure it), post-process layer (vkBasalt) and the gamescope micro-compositor. Also adds you to the gamemode group.
steps.check: rpm -q gamemode mangohud vkBasalt gamescope goverlay >/dev/null 2>&1
steps.run: dnf install -y gamemode mangohud vkBasalt gamescope goverlay && usermod -aG gamemode {USER}

steps.title: 3 · Install Protontricks
steps.desc: winetricks for Steam/Proton prefixes — used later to drop vcrun2005/xact/d3dx9 into Battlefront II's prefix if audio or video is missing, and to flip the prefix to Windows XP/7 if the launcher renders wrong.
steps.check: rpm -q protontricks >/dev/null 2>&1 || sudo -u {USER} flatpak info com.github.Matoking.protontricks >/dev/null 2>&1

steps.title: 4 · Install ProtonUp-Qt
steps.desc: GUI to manage GE-Proton / wine-GE versions per launcher. Installed as a Flatpak for {USER}. Old titles like this one sometimes run better on an older GE-Proton than on the newest Proton Experimental — this lets you keep several installed side by side.
steps.check: flatpak info net.davidotek.pupgui2 >/dev/null 2>&1 || sudo -u {USER} flatpak info net.davidotek.pupgui2 >/dev/null 2>&1
steps.run: dnf install -y flatpak && flatpak remote-add --if-not-exists flathub https://flathub.org/repo/flathub.flatpakrepo && sudo -u {USER} flatpak install -y --noninteractive flathub net.davidotek.pupgui2

steps.title: 5 · Install the latest GE-Proton
steps.desc: Downloads the newest GloriousEggroll GE-Proton release straight from GitHub and unpacks it into Steam's compatibilitytools.d for {USER}. Restart Steam afterwards so it shows up under Compatibility. If the newest GE-Proton doesn't get this game running, use ProtonUp-Qt (step 4) to also grab an older GE-Proton or plain Proton 7-8 — this title is old enough that a slightly older Proton sometimes behaves better than the newest one.
steps.run: su - {USER} -c 'set -e; d="$HOME/.local/share/Steam/compatibilitytools.d"; [ -d "$HOME/.steam/root" ] && d="$HOME/.steam/root/compatibilitytools.d"; mkdir -p "$d"; url=$(curl -fsSL https://api.github.com/repos/GloriousEggroll/proton-ge-custom/releases/latest | grep -oP "https://[^\x22]+GE-Proton[^\x22]+tar[.]gz" | head -1); test -n "$url"; echo "Downloading $url"; curl -fL "$url" -o /tmp/geproton.tar.gz; tar -xzf /tmp/geproton.tar.gz -C "$d"; rm -f /tmp/geproton.tar.gz; echo "compatibilitytools.d now holds:"; ls -1 "$d"'

steps.title: 5b · Keep the Proton prefix off NTFS / exFAT
steps.desc: If Star Wars Battlefront II lives on an NTFS or exFAT drive (common for a shared Windows game library), Proton can't build its prefix there — creating the drive-letter links dies with 'OSError: [Errno 22] … dosdevices/s:' because those filesystems reject ':' in a filename (ntfs3 'windows_names'), so the game never starts. Run step keeps the game where it is but moves just AppID {APPID}'s prefix onto your Linux drive and symlinks it back. Close Steam / the game first, then re-launch to rebuild the prefix cleanly. No-op if the game is already on a Linux filesystem.

steps.title: 6 · Enable Steam Play for all titles  (manual)
steps.desc: In Steam: Settings → Compatibility → turn on “Enable Steam Play for all other titles” and pick the GE-Proton from step 5. Restart Steam when it asks. This can't be scripted safely while Steam is running.

steps.title: 7 · Force a compatibility tool on Battlefront II  (manual)
steps.desc: Steam Library → right-click Star Wars Battlefront II → Properties → Compatibility → tick “Force the use of a specific Steam Play compatibility tool” → choose the GE-Proton from step 5. If it still won't launch, try a plain Proton 7 or 8 instead — this 2005 title sometimes runs worse on the newest Proton/GE-Proton than on an older one.

steps.title: 8 · Set the launch options  (manual)
steps.desc: Properties → General → Launch Options. Paste the string below (Copy button) — no anti-cheat here, so a plain gamemoderun mangohud %command% is enough. The three __…OFFLOAD / optimus / GLX vars render on the NVIDIA dGPU on the hybrid G15 — drop them if you've switched to nvidia-only graphics mode (Power & Limits → hybrid graphics). Build a fuller string (shader cache, gamescope, etc.) on the Game Tools tab's launch-options builder instead if you want more of those toggles.

steps.title: 9 · Crashes on the loading screen: wrap it in gamescope  (manual)
steps.desc: CONFIRMED fix for a reproducible crash on the G15: the game starts its Vulkan swapchain at 800×600, then resizes to the desktop resolution, and NVIDIA's proprietary driver segfaults recreating that swapchain (`vkDestroySwapchainKHR Exception 0xc0000005`, right after DXVK logs `Got VK_SUBOPTIMAL_KHR, recreating swapchain`) — captured with PROTON_LOG=1 in $HOME/steam-6060.log. gamescope (installed in step 2) gives the game one fixed-size surface up front so that resize — and the crash — never happens. Replace the launch options from step 8 with the string below (Copy button); `-f` runs gamescope fullscreen at your desktop's native resolution. TWO gotchas found the hard way on the G15: (1) the PRIME/NVIDIA env vars must go AFTER gamescope's `--` — putting them before gamescope forces gamescope's own nested Xwayland onto the NVIDIA-only vendor path too and crashes IT instead (xwl_glamor_init abort, falls back to a headless backend); (2) gamescope execs its child directly with no shell, so a bare `VAR=value` after `--` isn't parsed as an env assignment — it's tried as the program to run and fails ("No such file or directory") — `env` is what actually applies them.

steps.title: 10 · Still crashing: force wined3d  (manual)
steps.desc: If gamescope (step 9) doesn't fix it, add PROTON_USE_WINED3D=1 into the `env` list right after gamescope's `--` (same place as the other env vars) and relaunch. This bypasses DXVK/Vulkan for this title's legacy fixed-function Direct3D 9 renderer entirely (trading some speed for the older, more compatible OpenGL-backed wined3d path), so the NVIDIA Vulkan swapchain bug in step 9's description can't happen at all.

steps.title: 11 · Missing audio / video codecs  (manual)
steps.desc: Only needed if the intro movies don't play or menu audio is missing/crackly. Launch Battlefront II once first so Proton creates the prefix, quit, then run the command below (Copy) — it drops vcrun2005 and xact (DirectSound/XACT audio) into AppID {APPID}'s prefix non-interactively.

steps.title: 12 · First launch  (manual)
steps.desc: Start Star Wars Battlefront II from Steam. If the loading screen flashes and it dies, use step 9's gamescope launch string first — that's the confirmed fix for this game's crash on the G15. Still failing after that? Try step 10 (wined3d). For any other crash, enable PROTON_LOG=1 in the launch options (steam-6060.log lands in $HOME) so the real error can be pinned down instead of guessed at.

steps.title: 13 · Widescreen menus + stretched HUD  (manual)
steps.desc: This 2005 game's menus and Galactic Conquest screen are hardcoded to 800×600 — forcing a higher resolution makes gameplay render correctly (Hor+) but leaves menus pixelated/stretched and the HUD/crosshair misaligned (documented on PCGamingWiki). Two things fix it: (1) add a resolution launch argument (append it into the `env` list right after gamescope's `--`, alongside the other flags from step 9/10) — `-resolution 1920 1080` (swap in your desktop's actual resolution); this only works up to 16:9/16:10, which covers the G15's panel. (2) Install the community mod “Star Wars Battlefront II Remastered” (HD interface mod, ModDB) — it fixes the stretched/pixelated menus at forced resolutions, includes the Unofficial v1.3 Patch and AI Hero script, and adds a proper settings page (so don't also install v1.3 separately). Since it's a Windows installer, run it inside the same Proton prefix with protontricks-launch (Copy button below) — point it at the top-level “Star Wars Battlefront II Classic” folder when it asks, NOT the GameData or addon subfolder.

steps.title: 14 · Narrow field of view (FOV)  (manual)
steps.desc: The retail FOV is fixed and can feel narrow. The Unofficial v1.3 Patch (already included if you installed step 13's Remastered mod — install it standalone from ModDB otherwise) adds a “Fake Console”: pause the game in a match, open Fake Console from the pause menu, and set your FOV value there. Higher FOV values can show incomplete first-person hand/weapon models — that's a known limitation of the patch, not a sign something's broken.

OsuLazer.Description: osu!lazer is a native Linux build (AppImage), not a Steam/Proton game, so this card sets up osu-lazer-tools (github.com/BeanGreen247/osu-lazer-tools, bundled in TuxThrottle as the osu_lazer_tools module) instead of Steam launch options. Every launch goes through gamemoderun with the MangoHud overlay forced off (even though it's enabled globally) and: the power profile switched to performance and back, mouse acceleration flattened in KWin while playing, driver vsync off with a single pre-rendered frame and NVIDIA threaded-GL off, the persistent NVIDIA shader cache / DXVK state cache in TuxThrottle's shader-cache folder, and PipeWire pinned to a 256-frame quantum (~5 ms instead of the default 1024 = ~21 ms) so hitsounds line up. On the hybrid G15 it renders on the NVIDIA dGPU through PRIME offload (__NV_PRIME_RENDER_OFFLOAD / __VK_LAYER_NV_optimus / __GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME) with the OpenGL renderer. lazer updates itself in place from the main menu, so there is no update step. Work through the steps top to bottom.

steps.title: 1 · Install GameMode
steps.desc: The launcher refuses to start osu! without GameMode (gamemoderun). Also adds you to the gamemode group.

steps.title: 2 · Download osu!lazer + install the launcher
steps.desc: Reuses an osu! AppImage that's already set up (launcher config, ~/Applications, ~/Downloads, ~/.local/bin, ~) and otherwise downloads the latest release straight from github.com/ppy/osu into ~/Applications/osu.AppImage. Then installs ~/.local/bin/osu-lazer-launcher as a thin wrapper that runs TuxThrottle's own copy (so a TuxThrottle update reaches osu! with no re-install; your settings stay in ~/.config/osu-lazer-launcher/config) and adds “osu!” to the Games menu and the desktop, registered for osu:// links and .osz/.osk/.osr files. Close osu! first.

steps.title: 3 · Low-latency launcher config (dGPU, shader cache, audio, no overlay)
steps.desc: Writes the launcher config: USE_DGPU=yes (NVIDIA PRIME offload), SHADER_CACHE_DIR = TuxThrottle's shader-cache folder (Game Tools → Shader cache), LOW_LATENCY_AUDIO=yes with AUDIO_QUANTUM=256 (drop to 128 for less, raise to 512 if audio crackles) and PW_ALSA_TUNE=yes (pipewire-alsa buffer cut to 2 x 128 frames, per ppy/osu-framework#6647), SHOW_MANGOHUD=no (MangoHud stays off for osu!), FLAT_MOUSE=yes, PERFORMANCE_PROFILE=yes, DISABLE_DRIVER_VSYNC=yes. Edit ~/.config/osu-lazer-launcher/config to change any of them later.
steps.run: su - {USER} -c 'set -e; c=$HOME/.config/osu-lazer-launcher/config; sc=$(cd {TOOLKIT_DIR} && python3 -c "import tuxthrottle_shadercache as s; print(s.cache_dir())"); for kv in USE_DGPU=yes "SHADER_CACHE_DIR=\"$sc\"" LOW_LATENCY_AUDIO=yes AUDIO_QUANTUM=256 PW_ALSA_TUNE=yes ALSA_PERIOD_FRAMES=128 ALSA_PERIODS=2 SHOW_MANGOHUD=no FLAT_MOUSE=yes PERFORMANCE_PROFILE=yes DISABLE_DRIVER_VSYNC=yes; do k=${kv%%=*}; if grep -q "^$k=" "$c"; then sed -i "s|^$k=.*|$kv|" "$c"; else echo "$kv" >> "$c"; fi; done; ~/.local/bin/osu-lazer-launcher doctor'

steps.title: 4 · Let KWin tear for fullscreen games
steps.desc: Same as the KDE “allow screen tearing” tweak: kwinrc [Compositing] AllowTearing=true, so osu! in fullscreen can flip frames immediately instead of waiting for the compositor's next vblank. Only apps that ask for tearing are affected.
steps.run: sudo -u {USER} -H env XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/$(id -u {USER}) DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/user/$(id -u {USER})/bus bash -lc 'kwriteconfig6 --file kwinrc --group Compositing --key AllowTearing true; { qdbus-qt6 org.kde.KWin /KWin reconfigure || dbus-send --session --type=method_call --dest=org.kde.KWin /KWin org.kde.KWin.reconfigure; } 2>/dev/null || true'

steps.title: 5 · First launch  (manual)
steps.desc: Start osu! once from the Games menu (or run osu-lazer-launcher) so it creates its data folder, pick the OpenGL renderer under Settings → Graphics (the tested one for PRIME offload; the launcher warns if Vulkan is set), then quit. Crash output lands in ~/.cache/osu-lazer-launcher/last.log. The launcher falls back to the AMD iGPU automatically if the NVIDIA GL shaders fail to compile.

steps.title: 6 · Competitive game settings
steps.desc: Edits game.ini / framework.ini (backups next to each file): frame limiter Unlimited, fullscreen, multi-threaded execution, 100 % background dim, blur / hit lighting / star fountains / beatmap skins-colours-hitsounds off, key overlay on, in-game leaderboard off, mouse buttons + wheel disabled during play. Refuses while osu! is running (lazer rewrites both files on exit).

steps.title: 7 · Import skins / beatmaps  (manual)
steps.desc: Double-click a .osk skin or .osz beatmap (or drag it onto the osu! window) — step 2 registered the file types. Skin folders in ~/Downloads can be zipped and renamed to .osk first.

steps.title: 8 · Measure your mouse's real DPI  (manual, optional)
steps.desc: Needs evtest and sudo: move the mouse 10.16 cm three times and it prints the hardware DPI, so the in-game sensitivity can stay at 1.0 with raw input.

steps.title: 9 · Latency diagnostics  (manual, optional)
steps.desc: Live terminal dashboard of everything that adds latency: osu!'s real PipeWire quantum, xruns and ALSA buffer, an output-latency estimate, which GPU it renders on and whether it's throttling, osu!'s frame limiter / window mode, power profile, refresh rate + KWin tearing, mouse polling rate, IRQ / realtime priorities and the launcher config, each with what to change. Run it in a terminal while osu! is open (r refresh, s save report, q quit).
